title: PSC system reference: replacement fills for lost, stolen or damaged medication
content:
**Subject.** A Prescriptions & Renewals prescription may receive a replacement fill for medication the patient lost, had stolen or had damaged.

**Formal clauses.**

1. A replacement is authorized only where the prescription's class allows lost or stolen replacement and no replacement fill was posted on it in the rolling 12 months, never for a controlled prescription, and a stolen-medication replacement of a class that requires a police report carries the police report number exactly as the patient gives it.

2. A replacement fill's days' supply is fixed only after the prescription stands at a retail pharmacy rather than at a mail-order pharmacy.

2.1 Put the other way: while the prescription stands at a mail-order pharmacy, the days' supply of its replacement fill is not yet fixed. The pharmacy the prescription stands at is the one shown on the prescription record.

### Situation of use and capability

The tool posts one replacement fill authorization on a prescription for medication the patient lost, had stolen or had damaged. One call posts a single fill authorization with reason `replacement_fill`, dated today, for exactly one fill of the given days' supply, and raises the fills the prescription still authorizes by one; the pharmacy on the prescription can dispense that fill.

### How it is invoked

The tool is `authorize_replacement_fill_7c6c01e8`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `prescription_id` | reference number of the prescription the replacement is posted on, as shown by the prescription lookup for this patient | identifier |
| `days_supply_per_fill` | days' supply of the single replacement fill | whole number of days written as an integer greater than 0, no decimals and no unit text |
| `police_report_number` | police report number the patient gives for stolen medication | verbatim: copied exactly as the patient says it, every letter, digit and dash kept, nothing added or removed; left empty when the patient gives none |

The tool has no enumerated parameters; `police_report_number` may be left empty.

### Return

On success the receipt is a dictionary: `rx_event_id` (reference of the new replacement authorization entry), `prescription_id`, `fills` (always 1), `days_supply_per_fill` (integer days of the replacement fill), `authorization_reason` ("replacement_fill"), `fill_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `refills_remaining` (integer fills the prescription authorizes, this one included) and `status`, which reads "authorized" when the replacement is posted. Afterwards the fill history shows the new replacement authorization and the prescription lookup shows one more fill remaining. No other return or error is defined for the tool.

### Reading clause 1 (hypothetical cases)

| Situation | Clause 1 |
|---|---|
| Standard Maintenance Prescription, no replacement posted in the rolling 12 months | met |
| Same prescription with a replacement posted 8 months ago | not met |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | never |
| Specialty Medication Prescription, stolen medication, no replacement in the rolling 12 months | met, and the police report number is carried exactly as the patient gives it |
